messages:
tara: Heads-up — hit a weird micro-regression on live canary this morning. Small bursts (2-6 tokens) when KV cache is stored as INT8 show ~25-35% p99 tail latency increase vs FP8 baseline, even though memory drops ~18%. Also seeing occasional decode repetition artifacts on long contexts (1k+).

mike: Interesting. Do you have traces? Could be kernel selection churn when we flip between INT8/FP8 kernels in the same request path.

tara: Pasting the minimal trace from the canary node (timestamps are ms relative):
```
kv_lookup_start +0.0ms
kernel_select(INT8) +0.8ms
kv_dequantize +2.1ms
dispatch_kernel(INT8-kv-read) +0.3ms
kernel_select(FP8) +3.5ms <-- extra cost here when the decode path switches
decode_step +0.6ms
```
CPU-bound profiler shows many small kernel_select calls per token for these short bursts.

jin: That kernel_select jump (0.8 -> 3.5ms) screams hysteresis missing in routing. If the runtime picks kernels per-op with no sticky policy, mixed-precision workloads will thrash. We saw similar but smaller effects on medium batches. Two ideas: add per-request sticky kernel policy for N tokens OR introduce a sub-ms hysteresis window to avoid switching for ops within X ms.

sam: I ran a quick local sweep of batching/coalescing settings. Summary (canary vs two tweaks):
- baseline (FP8 KV): median 18ms, p95 42ms, p99 78ms, mem 1.00x, decode repros 0
- INT8 KV no-hysteresis: median 20ms, p95 45ms, p99 102ms, mem 0.82x, decode repros 3%
- INT8 KV + sticky-kernel(8 tokens): median 19ms, p95 43ms, p99 80ms, mem 0.83x, decode repros 1%
- INT8 KV + select-hysteresis(15ms): median 19.5ms, p95 44ms, p99 81ms, mem 0.83x, decode repros 0.8%
Conclusion: hysteresis or token-stickiness mostly recovers tail while keeping memory win.

tara: Nice numbers. The decode repros show subtle drift under INT8 calibration now. It looks like quantization noise accumulates when prefix KV is repeatedly dequantized/reused. Increasing the calibration window from 8->16 clips those tails in my quick test.

mike: Two follow-ups then: 1) Implement per-request kernel stickiness for the decode loop (config flag runtime.kv_precision.sticky_tokens = 8). 2) Add a soft hysteresis on kernel select that prefers current precision for X ms unless a heavier opcode forces a different kernel. Both should be cheap to implement and guarded behind a feature flag.

jin: Also propose we add a small micro-bench harness: run 1M 2-6 token bursts with mixed model traffic and collect kernel_select rate, kv_dequantize time, and quantization delta (log-likelihood delta on eval prompts). That will quantify quality vs perf tradeoffs.

sam: Quick config snippet for the canary to test tomorrow:
```
runtime_config:
  kv_precision:
    mode: int8-preferred
    sticky_tokens: 8
    select_hysteresis_ms: 15
  quant_calibration:
    window_tokens: 16
    calib_samples: 512
```
I'll spin it up on canary slot 3.

tara: Perfect. I'll collect p50/p95/p99 and run our existing eval set for decoding regressions after the canary stabilizes. If tails are back to baseline and no eval regressions, we can flip reserved nodes.

deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled: canary-slot-3 -> runtime-config-change at 1718456900. Watch logs: /infra/canary/slot-3/logs.

mike: I'll open a short task to instrument kernel_select latency in our tracing UI and add a dashboard tile. Ticket: RINF-3248.

tara: Thanks — adding test run notes to the ticket. Will report back with eval diffs + perf numbers in the morning. :thumbsup:
